content: I'll start by reading the test image to identify the symptoms.

This is a classic vascular/pith browning symptom. Top candidates: Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato, Verticillium_Wilt, Bacterial_Wilt, and Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers.

The Bacterial_Canker reference (Bugwood_13) confirms that this disease causes internal stem discoloration when the stem is cut open — consistent with the test image pattern. 

**Analysis summary:**
- **Test image**: Tomato stem split longitudinally at a branch junction, showing extensive brown/tan necrosis of the entire internal pith tissue, with intact green outer cortex
- **Alternaria (Bugwood_4)**: External dark/black stem canker at plant base — doesn't match
- **Verticillium Wilt (Bugwood_10)**: Shows leaf yellowing in whole plants — doesn't match
- **Bacterial Canker (Bugwood_13)**: Shows a stem cut open to reveal internal discoloration — matches the diagnostic approach and general symptom type

The complete brown pith necrosis running continuously along the stem (visible in a longitudinal split) is the hallmark diagnostic feature of **Bacterial Canker and Wilt of Tomato** (*Clavibacter michiganensis*). The pith turns brown/tan and necrotic while the outer cortex stays green, exactly matching the test image.
